name: Kakheti Qvevri Amber
description: Wine made the way it was eight thousand years ago: white grapes fermented on skins in clay qvevri buried to the neck in the earth, emerging amber and tannic.
funFact: Georgia has archaeological evidence of winemaking from around 6000 BC — the oldest yet found — and the qvevri method is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

serve.how: Serve cool but not cold, closer to a light red than a white — chilling shuts down the tannin and the wine tastes merely sour. Use a tulip rather than a large bowl. Expect grip and a tea-like tannin from the skin and stem contact; this is a food wine and works poorly on its own.

composition.summary: White grapes fermented and aged on skins in buried clay qvevri vessels.

components.label: Region
components.detail: Kakheti in eastern Georgia, the country's principal wine region.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Fermented on skins, stems and pips in qvevri buried underground.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: Up to six months on skins in the qvevri, then further ageing.

composition.process: Whole crushed grapes ferment with skins and stems in earth-buried clay vessels, where stable ground temperature drives a slow fermentation and long maceration.

name: Areni
description: High-altitude Armenian red from the Areni grape, grown near a cave that held a 6,100-year-old winery — the oldest ever excavated.
funFact: The Areni-1 cave in the same valley contained a wine press, fermentation vats and grape seeds dated to around 4100 BC — the oldest known winemaking facility anywhere in the world.

serve.how: Serve slightly cool in a large glass. Areni is naturally light in colour and high in acid — closer to Pinot Noir in weight than to a Georgian red — so do not judge it by depth of colour. A short decant helps young bottles; a long one strips them.

composition.summary: High-altitude indigenous Armenian red on volcanic soils at 1,400 metres and above.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Vayots Dzor province of southern Armenia, at high altitude on volcanic soil.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed and fermented moderately warm; some producers use karas clay vessels.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–18 months in oak or neutral clay.

composition.process: Extreme altitude with intense sun and cold nights ripens the fruit while holding acidity, giving pale but structured reds with a distinctly stony character.
